items.title: OpenTSLM: Language models that understand time series
items.raw_content: Paper: https://www.opentslm.com/OpenTSLM-whitepaper.pdf Repo: https://github.com/StanfordBDHG/OpenTSLM Foundation models excel at text, images, audio, and video, but lack temporal reasoning capabilities over time-series data streams that run the real world: vitals, prices, telemetry, grid loads, clickstreams, machine logs, business processes. Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) are open foundation models, supporting time‑series as a native modality, next to text, letting users ask questions, get explanations, and recommendations, all in natural language. The OpenTSLM White Paper released today demonstrates state-of-the-art temporal reasoning performance. Unlike prior approaches, the cross-attention architecture scales to long time-series remaining viable at scale. The results: - Sleep staging: 4.4× accuracy with a model 200× smaller (~880× efficiency) - Activity recognition: ~6× accuracy
items.title_zh: OpenTSLM：能理解时间序列的语言模型
items.summary: The OpenTSLM white paper presents open time-series language models that treat time series as a native modality alongside text, using a cross-attention architecture that scales to long sequences. The white paper reports 4.4x accuracy on sleep staging with a model 200x smaller and about 6x accuracy on activity recognition.

items.title: The RAG Obituary: Killed by agents, buried by context windows
items.raw_content: I’ve been working in AI and search for a decade. First, I built Doctrine, the largest European legal search engine, and now I am building Fintool , an AI-powered financial research platform that helps institutional investors analyze companies, screen stocks, and make investment decisions. After three years of building, optimizing, and scaling LLMs with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, I believe we’re witnessing the twilight of RAG-based architectures. As context windows explode and agent-based architectures mature, my controversial opinion is that the current RAG infrastructure we spent so much time building and optimizing is on the decline.
items.title_zh: RAG 讣告：被智能体杀死，被上下文窗口埋葬
items.summary: A developer who has spent three years building and scaling RAG systems argues that RAG-based architectures are in decline as context windows expand and agent-based architectures mature.

items.title: Show HN: Autism Simulator
items.raw_content: Hey all, I built this. It’s not trying to capture every autistic experience (that’d be impossible). It’s based on my own lived experience as well as that of friends on the spectrum. I'm trying to give people a feel for what masking, decision fatigue, and burnout can look like day-to-day. That’s hard to explain in words, but easier to show through choices and stats. I'm not trying to "define autism". I’ve gotten good feedback here about resilience, meds, and difficulty tuning. I’ll keep tweaking it. If even a few people walk away thinking, "ah, maybe that’s why my coworker struggles in those situations," then it’s worth it. Appreciate everyone who’s tried it and shared thoughts.
items.title_zh: Show HN：自闭症模拟器
items.summary: A developer built an interactive simulator, based on their own lived experience and that of friends on the spectrum, to convey what masking, decision fatigue, and burnout can feel like through choices and stats.
